title: Romeo and Juliet
author: d'après William Shakespeare
desc: Deux familles ennemies. Deux jeunes qui s'aiment. Une histoire qui finit mal.

p: In the beautiful city of Verona, in Italy, there were two rich and powerful families: the Montagues and the Capulets. They hated each other. Nobody remembered why. Their servants fought in the streets with swords.
Romeo was the son of Lord Montague. He was sixteen and always in love.
One night, the Capulets had a big party with masks. Romeo and his friends went secretly, with masks on their faces.
There, Romeo saw a girl dancing. She was more beautiful than the stars. "Did my heart love until now?" he said. "No. I never saw true beauty before tonight."
He talked to her. They kissed. Then he learned her name: Juliet. Juliet Capulet. The daughter of his enemy.
Romeo couldn't go home. He climbed the wall of the Capulet garden. Juliet was on her balcony, in the moonlight.
"O Romeo, Romeo, why are you Romeo?" she said, not knowing he was there. "What's in a name? A rose with any other name would smell as sweet."
Romeo came out of the shadows. "Call me 'love', and I will never be Romeo again."
They promised to marry. The next day, a friendly priest, Friar Laurence, married them in secret. He hoped the marriage would end the war between the two families.
But that same afternoon, Juliet's cousin Tybalt attacked Romeo's best friend Mercutio and killed him. Romeo was furious. He fought Tybalt and killed him.
The Prince of Verona banished Romeo from the city. If he came back, he would die.
Romeo went to the city of Mantua. Juliet cried day and night.
Then her father announced: "In three days, you will marry Count Paris!"
Juliet ran to Friar Laurence. "Help me, or I will kill myself!"

The friar gave her a small bottle. "Drink this tonight. You will sleep so deeply that everyone will think you are dead. They will put you in the family tomb. I will send a letter to Romeo. He will come, and when you wake up, you will leave together."
Juliet drank it. In the morning, her family found her cold and still. They cried and put her in the tomb.
But the friar's letter never arrived. Instead, Romeo's servant came to Mantua with terrible news: "Juliet is dead."
Romeo bought poison and rode back to Verona at night. In the tomb, he saw Juliet. She looked so beautiful, as if she was sleeping.
"Here I will stay with you forever," he said. He kissed her one last time and drank the poison.
A few minutes later, Juliet woke up. She saw Romeo dead next to her, with the empty bottle in his hand.
"Poison? You drank it all and left nothing for me?" She kissed his lips, hoping for a little poison. Then she took his dagger. "O happy dagger," she said, and she killed herself.
In the morning, the two families found their children, dead together. Lord Montague and Lord Capulet looked at each other. They cried and finally shook hands.
Their hatred had killed the people they loved most. As the Prince said: "There was never a story of more sadness than this of Juliet and her Romeo."
